To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucocorticoids stimulate the rat GHR-receptor gene transcription in the presence of pit-1, and that pit-1 suppresses the activity of a silencer that is present in the promoter.
pit-1 is involved in the regulation by glucocorticoid of the rat growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GH-RH) receptor gene transcription.

glucocorticoids are not capable of activating the rat growth hormone releasing hormone receptor gene transcription, but they can do so when the transcription factor, pituitary specific protein-1, is present, and that the distance between the glucocorticoids response element and the binding site of pit-1 affects the synergistic activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanism of the glucocorticoids action on the GHRH receptor gene transcription.
the identification of a novel pit-1-dependent glucocorticoid responsive element in the rat GHR-receptor gene promoter and the characterization of the mechanism of the pit-1 action.
the role of pituitary-specific transcription factor in the regulation of GHRH-receptors in rat pituitary.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

glucocorticoids are not the sole factor that regulates the GHRH receptor gene expression, and that pit-1 is involved in the synergistic activation and glucocorticoid-mediated regulation of the rat GRR gene.
glucocorticoid receptor and pit-1 interact to activate transcription of the GHRR gene.
pit-1 is a necessary coactivator for the synergistic glucocorticoid effect on the rat GHRR-receptor gene transcription.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pit-1 is a necessary factor for the glucocorticoids to act on the GHRH receptor gene transcription.
pit-1 is required for the glucocorticoids to stimulate the rat GHRR gene transcription.
glucocorticoid receptor (GR) and pit-1 are involved in the transcriptional activation of the GHR receptor gene, which is mediated by the glucocorticoids and pit-1, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the synergism of pit-1 and glucocorticoids in the regulation of GHRH receptor gene expression is a result of a complex interplay between the pit-1, glucocorticoid receptor, and an as yet unknown silencer factor.
pit-1 is required for the glucocorticoids to stimulate the rat GHR-receptor gene transcription.
the pit-1 factor is required for the glucocorticoids to exert their stimulatory effect on the GHRH receptor gene transcription.
